methodology.outcomeRule: A market counts as resolved when the graph marks it closed/resolved, or when its end date falls on the report's UTC day or earlier while its YES odds are terminal. The projected basis instead admits every market at terminal odds, regardless of flags or end date. On either basis a forecast is scored NO only when terminal YES odds are strictly below 1%, and YES only when strictly above 99%; values exactly at 1% or 99% are excluded.
methodology.brierDefinition: Mean squared error between the probability stated at forecast time and the report outcome; lower is better and 0.25 is the always-50% baseline.
methodology.qAdvantageDefinition: Market-at-forecast Brier minus Quotient Brier; positive means Quotient was more accurate on that sample.
methodology.accuracyDefinition: qAccuracy is the share of observations where the market resolved on Quotient's side — the stated probability sat on the winning side of 50%, with exactly 50% never counting as right. marketAccuracy applies the same rule to the market-at-forecast price. On mean_per_market the compared probability is the market's mean stated probability. Directional accuracy ignores confidence, so read it with the Brier comparison.
methodology.benchmarkDefinition: The market YES probability stored with each forecast at creation time, regardless of the market's current price.
methodology.returnDefinition: Hypothetical purchase of the side Quotient considered underpriced, using the market price stored at forecast creation; no fees, spread crossing, slippage, sizing, or overlapping-position constraints.

bases.resolved: Markets explicitly flagged closed/resolved, plus markets at terminal odds whose end date is on or before the report's UTC day. This is the reporting default.
bases.projected: Every market at terminal YES odds (strictly below 1% or above 99%), including still-open ones, scored as if it settles the way its price points. A leading view, not settled history.

scopes.all_markets: Every valid forecast on a market with a binary terminal outcome, filtered per basis.
scopes.geopolitics_global_elections: Eligible forecasts whose market Event has a geopolitics or global elections tag.

periods.all_time: Every eligible forecast in the selected scope and basis.
periods.last_60_days: Eligible forecasts created in the 60 days before generatedAt.

samples.mean_per_market: Each market is one observation scored on the mean Brier of every eligible forecast on it, so each market counts once regardless of forecast volume.
samples.one_random_per_market: One reproducibly selected forecast per market using a fixed SHA-256 key — a per-market robustness check on the mean view.

reporting.context: Geopolitics and global elections are Quotient's most consistently forecasted categories, so that scope is the primary reporting cohort. Each period also includes all markets without the category filter. Every reported view weights each market once: mean_per_market (the primary) scores a market on the mean Brier of its forecasts, and one_random_per_market is its reproducibly sampled robustness check. samples score the resolved basis (explicitly flagged, or ended with terminal odds); projected repeats them counting every terminal-odds market as if it settles the way its price points.

caveats: This is retrospective context, not a live promise or investment advice.

The resolved basis no longer waits for the graph's closed/resolved flag when a market's end date has passed and its odds are terminal; a wrong or stale end date can therefore admit a market before it truly settles.
The projected basis counts still-open markets at terminal odds as if they resolve the way the price points; a late reversal would rewrite those rows. Treat projected as a leading indicator.
The binary outcome is mapped from terminal YES odds on both bases; markets without odds strictly below 1% or above 99% are excluded entirely.
Both reported samples weight each market once, so repeatedly-forecast markets do not dominate the averages; per-forecast weighting is intentionally not reported.

Directional accuracy (qAccuracy, marketAccuracy) is flattered by lopsided markets — calling a 95% market counts the same as calling a coin flip — so compare the two accuracies and the Brier scores together rather than quoting one accuracy alone.
Recent cohorts are incomplete because the last-60-day resolved view includes only forecasts whose markets already count as resolved.
Percentage returns can be highly skewed for inexpensive shares; inspect medians, sample counts, and positiveShare with means.
Seven-day coverage here uses graph-stored marketPriceAt7d or delta7d only; the Marimo notebook may cover additional rows from its local companion CLOB cache.
